title: Azure Blob Storage Access Tiers
text: Azure Blob Storage provides four access tiers for block blobs: hot, cool, cold and archive. The hot tier is optimised for frequently accessed data and has the highest storage cost but the lowest access cost. The cool tier suits infrequently accessed data stored for at least 30 days. The cold tier is for rarely accessed data stored for at least 90 days. The archive tier offers the lowest storage cost but is offline; data must be rehydrated to an online tier before it can be read, which can take several hours.

title: Azure Storage Redundancy Options
text: Azure Storage offers several redundancy options. Locally redundant storage (LRS) keeps three copies of data within a single datacentre and provides at least eleven nines of durability. Zone-redundant storage (ZRS) replicates data synchronously across three availability zones in a region. Geo-redundant storage (GRS) replicates to a paired secondary region for sixteen nines of durability. Geo-zone-redundant storage (GZRS) combines zone redundancy in the primary region with geo-replication to the secondary region.

title: Azure Virtual Machine Availability SLA
text: Azure offers a financially backed service level agreement of 99.99 percent for virtual machines deployed across two or more availability zones in a region. For two or more instances in the same availability set the SLA is 99.95 percent. For a single virtual machine using premium SSD or Ultra Disk for all operating system and data disks the SLA is 99.9 percent. Availability sets protect against rack-level hardware failures within a single datacentre.

title: Azure Availability Zones, Sets and Regions
text: An Azure region is a set of datacentres deployed within a latency-defined perimeter. Availability zones are physically separate locations within a region, each with independent power, cooling and networking, protecting against datacentre-level failure. Availability sets protect only against rack-level and host failures within a single datacentre. Region pairs provide geo-replication and disaster recovery across a large distance.

title: Azure Virtual Machine Scale Sets
text: Virtual Machine Scale Sets let you create and manage a group of load-balanced virtual machines. The number of instances can automatically increase or decrease in response to demand or a defined schedule through autoscale rules based on metrics such as CPU usage. Scale sets support up to 1000 instances and integrate with Azure Load Balancer and Application Gateway.

title: Azure App Service Plans
text: Azure App Service is a fully managed platform for hosting web applications and APIs. The App Service plan defines the compute resources and pricing tier. Scaling up changes the size of the underlying compute, while scaling out adds more instances. The Premium and Isolated tiers support autoscaling and deployment slots for staged releases and zero-downtime swaps.

title: Azure Functions Hosting Plans and Triggers
text: Azure Functions is a serverless compute service. The Consumption plan scales automatically and to zero when idle, billing only for execution time and memory. The Premium plan provides pre-warmed instances that eliminate cold starts and support virtual network connectivity. Functions are invoked by triggers including HTTP requests, timers, and messages on queues, blobs, Event Hubs and Service Bus.

title: Azure Container Apps
text: Azure Container Apps is a serverless container platform built on Kubernetes and the open-source KEDA, Dapr and Envoy projects. It supports event-driven autoscaling, including scaling to zero when there is no traffic, based on HTTP traffic or event sources. It abstracts away cluster management, unlike Azure Kubernetes Service which exposes the Kubernetes API directly.

title: Azure Kubernetes Service
text: Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) is a managed Kubernetes offering where Azure manages the control plane at no charge and you pay only for the agent nodes. A cluster uses one or more node pools; a system node pool hosts critical system pods while user node pools run application workloads. The cluster autoscaler adds or removes nodes based on pending pods.

title: Azure Container Registry
text: Azure Container Registry (ACR) is a managed private Docker registry for storing and managing container images and artefacts. It offers Basic, Standard and Premium service tiers; the Premium tier adds geo-replication, private link support and higher throughput. ACR Tasks can build and patch images in the cloud.

title: Azure Load Balancer versus Application Gateway
text: Azure Load Balancer operates at layer 4 of the OSI model and distributes inbound TCP and UDP traffic based on a five-tuple hash. Application Gateway operates at layer 7 and can route HTTP requests based on URL path or host header, terminate TLS, and provides an integrated Web Application Firewall. Use Load Balancer for non-HTTP workloads and Application Gateway for web traffic that needs content-based routing.

title: Azure Application Gateway and Web Application Firewall
text: Application Gateway is a layer 7 load balancer for web traffic supporting URL-based routing, cookie-based session affinity and TLS termination. Its optional Web Application Firewall protects applications against common exploits such as SQL injection and cross-site scripting using the OWASP core rule set.

title: Azure Virtual Network and Subnets
text: An Azure Virtual Network (VNet) is a logically isolated network in the cloud. It is defined by one or more address spaces in CIDR notation and divided into subnets. Resources in the same VNet can communicate by default, and VNets can be connected with peering. Subnets segment the address space and can have route tables and network security groups applied.

title: Network Security Groups
text: A Network Security Group (NSG) filters inbound and outbound traffic to Azure resources using security rules. Each rule has a priority between 100 and 4096; rules are evaluated in priority order and a lower number has higher precedence. The first matching rule applies. NSGs include default rules that deny all inbound traffic from the internet unless explicitly allowed.

title: Azure Private Link and Private Endpoints
text: Azure Private Link enables access to Azure PaaS services over a private endpoint inside your virtual network. A private endpoint is a network interface assigned a private IP address from your subnet, so traffic to the service travels over the Microsoft backbone rather than the public internet, reducing exposure to data exfiltration.

title: Azure ExpressRoute versus VPN Gateway
text: ExpressRoute provides a private, dedicated connection between on-premises infrastructure and Azure through a connectivity provider; the traffic does not traverse the public internet, offering higher reliability and lower latency. A VPN Gateway establishes an encrypted tunnel over the public internet. ExpressRoute is preferred for predictable performance and large or sensitive workloads.

title: Azure Front Door
text: Azure Front Door is a global, scalable entry point that uses the Microsoft global edge network to deliver and accelerate web applications. It provides global HTTP load balancing, TLS offload, caching, and a Web Application Firewall at the edge, routing users to the lowest-latency healthy backend.

title: Azure DNS and Traffic Manager
text: Azure DNS hosts DNS domains and resolves names using Microsoft infrastructure. Azure Traffic Manager is a DNS-based traffic load balancer that distributes traffic across global endpoints using routing methods such as priority, weighted, performance and geographic, improving availability and responsiveness.

title: Microsoft Entra ID and Role-Based Access Control
text: Azure role-based access control (RBAC) grants access through role assignments that combine a security principal, a role definition and a scope. Scopes are hierarchical: management group, subscription, resource group and resource, and assignments are inherited downward. Built-in roles include Owner, Contributor and Reader; Owner can manage access while Contributor cannot.

title: Azure Managed Identities
text: A managed identity provides an automatically managed identity in Microsoft Entra ID for applications to use when connecting to resources that support Entra authentication, removing the need to store credentials in code. System-assigned identities are tied to a resource lifecycle, while user-assigned identities are standalone and can be shared across multiple resources.

title: Azure Key Vault
text: Azure Key Vault is a managed service for securely storing and accessing secrets, keys and certificates. It supports soft-delete and purge protection to guard against accidental or malicious deletion, and access can be controlled with RBAC or access policies. Keys can be backed by software or by FIPS 140-2 validated hardware security modules in the Premium tier.

title: Microsoft Defender for Cloud
text: Microsoft Defender for Cloud is a cloud security posture management and cloud workload protection platform. It continuously assesses resources against security best practices and expresses the result as a secure score, provides hardening recommendations, and offers threat protection for workloads such as servers, storage, databases and containers.

title: Microsoft Sentinel
text: Microsoft Sentinel is a cloud-native security information and event management (SIEM) and security orchestration, automation and response (SOAR) solution. It collects security data at scale across the enterprise, detects threats using analytics rules and the Kusto Query Language, and automates response with playbooks built on Azure Logic Apps.

title: Azure Policy and Governance
text: Azure Policy enforces organisational standards and assesses compliance at scale. Policy definitions describe resource conditions and an effect such as deny, audit or deployIfNotExists. Initiatives group related policies, and assignments apply them to a scope. Policy complements RBAC: RBAC controls who can act, while Policy controls what resources are allowed.

title: Azure Monitor and Log Analytics
text: Azure Monitor collects and analyses telemetry across applications and infrastructure as metrics and logs. Logs are stored in a Log Analytics workspace and queried with the Kusto Query Language (KQL). Alert rules can fire on metric thresholds or log query results and trigger action groups for notification or automation.

title: Application Insights
text: Application Insights is the application performance monitoring feature of Azure Monitor. It automatically collects request rates, response times, failure rates, dependency calls and exceptions, and provides distributed tracing, live metrics and an application map to diagnose performance issues in web applications and services.

title: Azure Backup
text: Azure Backup provides centralised backup for virtual machines, files, databases and on-premises workloads, storing recovery points in a Recovery Services vault. It supports configurable retention policies and offers geo-redundant storage for backup data, along with soft delete to protect recovery points against accidental deletion.

title: Azure Site Recovery
text: Azure Site Recovery orchestrates disaster recovery by replicating workloads to a secondary region and enabling failover and failback. The recovery point objective (RPO) is the maximum acceptable data loss measured in time, while the recovery time objective (RTO) is the maximum acceptable time to restore service. Recovery plans automate multi-tier failover.

title: Azure Cost Management and Budgets
text: Microsoft Cost Management provides tools to monitor, allocate and optimise Azure spending. Cost analysis breaks down spend by dimensions such as resource group, service and tag. Budgets set spending thresholds that trigger alerts when actual or forecast cost crosses configured percentages, helping teams avoid overspend.

title: Infrastructure as Code with Bicep and ARM Templates
text: Azure Resource Manager (ARM) templates and the Bicep language describe Azure infrastructure declaratively for repeatable deployments. Bicep is a more concise domain-specific language that compiles to ARM JSON. Deployments are idempotent: applying the same template repeatedly converges to the same desired state without creating duplicate resources.

title: Azure SQL Database Purchasing Models
text: Azure SQL Database is a managed relational database offering two purchasing models. The DTU model bundles compute, storage and I/O into a single blended unit across Basic, Standard and Premium tiers. The vCore model lets you choose the number of virtual cores and memory independently and supports the Hyperscale and serverless options for elastic scaling.

title: Azure Cosmos DB Consistency Levels
text: Azure Cosmos DB is a globally distributed, multi-model database offering five well-defined consistency levels: strong, bounded staleness, session, consistent prefix and eventual. Session consistency is the default and guarantees a client reads its own writes. Stronger consistency increases latency and cost, while weaker consistency improves availability and throughput.

title: Vector Search in Azure Cosmos DB
text: Azure Cosmos DB supports vector search by storing embedding vectors alongside documents and indexing them for similarity search. This integrated vector store lets applications combine operational data and semantic search in a single database, which is useful for retrieval-augmented generation over operational records without a separate vector database.

title: Azure Storage Account Services
text: An Azure storage account provides a namespace for several data services: Blob (object) storage, Azure Files (SMB and NFS file shares), Queue storage for messaging, and Table storage for NoSQL key-value data. The general-purpose v2 account is recommended for most scenarios and supports all tiers and redundancy options.

title: Azure Data Factory
text: Azure Data Factory is a managed cloud data-integration service for building extract-transform-load and extract-load-transform pipelines. Pipelines contain activities that move and transform data; the copy activity ingests from many sources, and mapping data flows run transformations on managed Spark clusters without writing code.

title: Azure Synapse Analytics
text: Azure Synapse Analytics is an integrated analytics service that brings together data warehousing and big-data processing. It provides dedicated and serverless SQL pools, Apache Spark pools, and integrated pipelines, allowing analysts to query data at scale using either SQL or Spark within a single workspace.

title: Azure Databricks
text: Azure Databricks is an Apache Spark-based analytics platform optimised for Azure, used for large-scale data engineering, data science and machine learning. It provides collaborative notebooks, managed Spark clusters, and the Delta Lake storage layer that adds ACID transactions and schema enforcement to data lakes.

title: Azure Event Hubs
text: Azure Event Hubs is a big-data streaming platform and event ingestion service that can receive and process millions of events per second. Data is organised into partitions for parallel consumption, and consumer groups allow multiple independent reading applications. It supports an Apache Kafka-compatible endpoint.

title: Azure Service Bus
text: Azure Service Bus is an enterprise message broker supporting queues for point-to-point communication and topics with subscriptions for publish-subscribe patterns. It guarantees ordered, at-least-once delivery, supports sessions for ordered processing and dead-letter queues for messages that cannot be delivered, decoupling application components.

title: Azure AI Search Hybrid Retrieval
text: Azure AI Search is a managed search service that supports full-text keyword search using BM25 scoring and vector search over embeddings. Hybrid search runs both keyword and vector queries and fuses their result sets using Reciprocal Rank Fusion, combining exact-term matching with semantic similarity in a single query.

title: Azure AI Search Semantic Ranker
text: The semantic ranker in Azure AI Search re-scores an initial set of results using deep learning models to promote the most contextually relevant documents and can return concise extractive captions and answers. It is applied as a second-stage reranking step on top of keyword or hybrid retrieval to improve precision at the top of the ranking.

title: Azure OpenAI Service
text: Azure OpenAI Service provides REST API access to OpenAI models, including the GPT-4 family for generation and the text-embedding models, hosted within Azure with enterprise security, regional availability and compliance. Models are accessed through deployments created in an Azure OpenAI resource, each mapping a model version to a deployment name.

title: Azure OpenAI Embedding Models
text: Azure OpenAI offers embedding models that convert text into dense numeric vectors for semantic search and retrieval. The text-embedding-3-small model produces 1536-dimensional vectors, while text-embedding-3-large produces 3072-dimensional vectors with higher accuracy. Both support shortening the dimension count to trade accuracy for storage and speed.

title: Azure OpenAI Quota and Provisioned Throughput
text: Azure OpenAI usage is governed by quota expressed in tokens-per-minute (TPM), which is allocated per region and per model and can be distributed across deployments. For predictable high-volume workloads, Provisioned Throughput Units (PTUs) reserve dedicated capacity that delivers stable latency and throughput independent of other tenants.

title: Azure AI Content Safety
text: Azure AI Content Safety detects harmful content in text and images across four categories: hate, sexual, violence and self-harm. Each detection returns a severity level so applications can apply thresholds and block or escalate content. It also offers prompt-shield detection for jailbreak and indirect prompt-injection attacks.

title: Azure Machine Learning Workspace
text: Azure Machine Learning is a platform for the end-to-end machine learning lifecycle. The workspace is the top-level resource that holds compute, datastores, models, environments and experiments. It supports training with the SDK or designer, model registration and versioning, and MLOps pipelines for repeatable training and deployment.

title: Azure Machine Learning Managed Endpoints
text: Azure Machine Learning managed online endpoints serve models for real-time, low-latency inference over HTTPS, handling provisioning, scaling and TLS. Deployments under an endpoint allow safe rollout strategies such as blue-green by splitting traffic between versions. Batch endpoints serve asynchronous scoring over large datasets.

title: Azure AI Document Intelligence
text: Azure AI Document Intelligence, formerly Form Recognizer, extracts text, key-value pairs, tables and structure from documents using optical character recognition and machine learning. Prebuilt models handle invoices, receipts and identity documents, while custom models can be trained on an organisation's own forms, providing structured input for retrieval pipelines.

title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation Overview
text: Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) conditions a language model on passages retrieved from an external knowledge base at inference time rather than relying solely on parametric knowledge. By grounding answers in retrieved evidence, RAG reduces factual errors and hallucination and allows responses to reflect current, organisation-specific information without retraining the model.

title: Chunking Strategies for RAG
text: Documents are split into smaller chunks before embedding so that retrieval returns focused, relevant passages. Fixed-size token windows with a small overlap are common; larger chunks preserve context but dilute relevance, while smaller chunks improve precision but may lose surrounding meaning. Overlap prevents information being split awkwardly across chunk boundaries.

title: Hybrid Retrieval and Reciprocal Rank Fusion
text: Hybrid retrieval combines sparse lexical retrieval such as BM25 with dense vector retrieval to capture both exact-term matches and semantic similarity. Because the two methods produce incomparable score scales, their ranked lists are commonly merged with Reciprocal Rank Fusion, which sums the reciprocal of each item's rank across lists and is robust to differing score ranges.

title: Reranking in RAG Pipelines
text: A reranking stage reorders an initial candidate set to improve precision at the top of the ranking. A cross-encoder reranker jointly encodes the query and each candidate passage to produce a relevance score, which is more accurate than the bi-encoder similarity used for first-stage retrieval but more computationally expensive, so it is applied only to the top candidates.

title: Grounding and Citations for Verifiability
text: Citation-grounded generation requires the model to attribute each claim to the retrieved passage that supports it, making answers auditable in regulated settings. Citations do not by themselves guarantee correctness, because a system may cite irrelevant passages, so citation coverage and the rate of invalid citations are measured to quantify verifiability.

title: Evaluating RAG with RAGAS
text: RAGAS is a framework for automated evaluation of retrieval-augmented generation. Faithfulness measures the proportion of answer claims grounded in the retrieved context and is the primary hallucination indicator. Answer relevance measures how well the answer addresses the question, context recall measures coverage of the reference, and answer correctness compares the answer with a reference answer.

title: Responsible AI and Enterprise Governance
text: Enterprise AI operations apply governance across the model lifecycle, including responsible-AI assessment, human oversight, monitoring for drift and abuse, and controls for data residency and privacy. Keeping data within approved regions, logging prompts and outputs for audit, and restricting access through identity controls help organisations deploy generative AI in a compliant and accountable way.
